wave_title: Following two duplicate-classification-logic fixes earlier this session (persistence.rs's Expr::Call/MethodCall spelling match, and is_panic_like_macro duplicated across cfg.rs/effect.rs), wrote a small Python script to systematically find every cross-file exact-duplicate function body (normalized whitespace, >=60 chars, skipping test modules) across core/adapter/runtime/apps-cli. Found three more real instances: state.rs's private is_compound_assignment duplicating spelling.rs's already-shared is_compound_assign_op (dataflow.rs's own doc comment already referenced the shared version, implying state.rs was meant to use it too but never did), and a cross-CRATE duplication (core::graph::engineering_graph and runtime::census::mod each independently defining byte-for-byte-identical scoped_identity/scoped_name and function_signature_identity/function_signature_summary functions).

priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity (priority 1) -- the cross-crate instance (core/runtime) is the most significant found this session: two crates independently maintaining the same graph-node-identity-string and function-signature-summary logic, where core's copy feeds EngineeringGraph node identities and runtime's copy feeds the bootstrap SemanticFact.object compatibility projection of the SAME underlying data. A future edit to either copy alone would make the typed graph and the compatibility-fact projection describe the same symbol differently, a genuine cross-representation consistency risk.

design_decisions.question: For the cross-crate duplication, keep both as private free functions (one per crate) calling into a newly-shared crate-level helper, or promote to inherent methods on the core types themselves?
design_decisions.decision: Inherent methods: `SemanticScope::scoped_name(&self, name: &str) -> String` (alongside the type's existing `new`/`join` methods) and `FunctionSignature::summary(&self) -> String` (a fresh `impl FunctionSignature` block, previously absent), both in `core::semantic`. This is the natural, idiomatic Rust home for logic that operates purely on one type's own fields, matches `SemanticScope`'s own existing `join()` convention exactly, and gives `runtime` (which already depends on `core`) and `core::graph::engineering_graph` itself the same single call path with no new free-function indirection layer to maintain.

design_decisions.question: Rename `function_signature_identity`/`function_signature_summary` (they disagreed on name) to something new, or pick one of the two existing names?
design_decisions.decision: `summary`, not `identity` -- deliberately avoiding the more common of the two existing names because the string this method returns is explicitly NOT a canonical/compiler-resolved identity (`TypeIdentity.canonical` stays `None` throughout this whole kernel); calling it `identity` risked a future reader mistaking it for a real identity computation. `summary` accurately describes what it is: a source-spelling display string.
